title: Introduction to stackcallr
text: ’re reading unfamiliar code, one first questions : function actually call? simple function can just read body. S3 generic like dplyr::select(), body single line, UseMethod("select"), real work happens method ’d go find . stackcallr answers question directly. Give call_stack() name function, returns tree every function calls, functions call, , resolving S3 dispatch along way.

title: Introduction to stackcallr
text: Static analysis alone can’t tell UseMethod("select") actually runs, since depends class argument call time. call_stack() handles case specifically: function’s body calls UseMethod(), looks every method registered generic follows one, place single unhelpful UseMethod leaf. mean.* entry real method, resolved ready expanded larger max_depth.

what: Build the call tree of a function — call_stack
title: Build the call tree of a function — call_stack
text: call_stack() takes name function, optionally namespaced (e.g. "dplyr::select"), statically parses body, recursively resolves every function calls, building tree calls, calls functions make, . Resolution static (read function's source code), runtime trace: function never called. UseMethod() dispatch resolved looking generic's registered S3 methods following one. dynamic calls (NextMethod(), S4 R6 dispatch, non-standard evaluation) show leaves rather followed .
